feed.title: The Sample Kitchen Journal
feed.subtitle: Plain cooking notes for weeknight meals. A fixture feed invented for this guide's lab.

entry.title: A sharper knife is a safer knife
entry.summary: A dull knife slips; a sharp one goes where you point it. A few strokes on a steel before you start, and a proper sharpening a few times a year, is the whole secret.

entry.title: Stock from the freezer bag
entry.summary: Keep a bag in the freezer for onion ends, carrot tops and herb stems. When the bag is full, cover the contents with water, simmer for an hour, and strain. Stock from scraps costs nothing and tastes like it.

entry.title: The five-minute pan sauce
entry.summary: After frying, the pan holds the flavour. Pour in a glass of water or wine, scrape the browned bits loose as it bubbles, and finish with a knob of butter. Five minutes turns plain into finished.

entry.title: Salting pasta water, honestly
entry.summary: About a tablespoon of salt per litre of water, added when the water boils. The pasta is seasoned from the inside, and a cup of the starchy water loosens any sauce. That is the entire trick.
